PANEL 2 — THE BRONCHIAL BRANCHING
The tunnel divides into two smaller passages opening away from the lens in a Y. The walls are narrower and softer than the trachea, the cartilage now irregular plates rather than full rings, the lining dense with fine red capillary lace and carrying a visible carpet of microscopic cilia lying in soft waves. PANEL 3 — ARRIVAL AT THE ALVEOLI
A narrow bronchiole opening into a wide alveolar chamber. The passage walls are very thin and highly translucent, backlit so the capillary network reads as a dense red-amber lace running through them. Beyond the opening, hundreds of thin-walled alveolar sacs cluster like a honeycomb of soft rounded chambers, each slightly different in size and shape, each glowing warm amber from within, separated by pale translucent septal walls. PANEL 4 — OVER-INFLATION
Full frame on the alveolar cluster from close above, and every sac has swollen far beyond its natural size. The chambers are stretched taut and rounded, pressing hard against one another and deforming where they meet, the septal walls between them squeezed thin and flattened. Each wall is stretched so thin it has become almost transparent, the amber glow blazing through more brightly than before because there is less tissue to pass through. The capillary networks are pulled taut and spread far apart across the expanded surfaces, the fine vessels stretched into long thin lines and visibly blanching where they thin. The whole cluster is under visible tension and strain, trembling at the limit. Nothing has failed yet. This is the brightest and most tense panel — beauty at the point of breaking.

PANEL 5 — FAILURE AND DARKENING
The same cluster moments later. Many of the over-stretched sacs have given way — their thin walls opened along irregular seams and collapsed inward, the slackened tissue folded and creased into crumpled hollows where rounded chambers used to be. The failure is uneven and ragged, spreading in an irregular branched pattern rather than a clean circle.
